text:
michael: heads-up — we started seeing prod inference nodes fail to resolve redis.prod.internal this morning, ~30% of requests got DNS NXDOMAIN from within the VPC

sara: same, symptoms look like split-horizon DNS. service name maps to an interface endpoint but Route53 is returning the wrong hosted zone

leo: digging in — dig output from one affected node: ```$ dig +short redis.prod.internal @10.0.0.2
10.55.132.21
```

leo: but that IP is an old A record in a shared private hosted zone owned by infra-account, not the interface endpoint ENI IPs we expect

infra-oncall: alert from kubernetes healthcheck: "redis resolution failed: NXDOMAIN" on 8 pods across two AZs, started 06:07 UTC

michael: timeline: rolled a small route-table update at 05:50 UTC to add a propagation to the NAT VPC peer — maybe coincident but seems DNS-only so far

oliver: checked endpoint config: InterfaceEndpoint id vpce-0a1b2c3d has PrivateDnsEnabled=true, should create records in the VPC's private hosted zone (AWS-managed). But if there's a PHZ with same zone name in another account that can override resolver answers if associations are different

leo: aws-bot: ```aws route53 list-hosted-zones-by-name --dns-name "prod.internal"``` returned two zones: ZONE-A (account infra) and ZONE-B (account services). ZONE-A has A record for redis.prod.internal -> 10.55.132.21 (stale). ZONE-B has the alias to vpce-eni IPs but currently not associated to this VPC

infra-oncall: @sara can you confirm resolver rule priority? we might have an outbound resolver rule that prefers the infra-account PHZ via conditional forwarding

sara: confirmed — we have a Route53Resolver rule (svc-forward-prod) that points to the infra-account resolver endpoint and it has higher priority than the VPC's default. That explains why nodes hit the infra PHZ first

michael: why did this start now though? there was a stale A record that should've existed but traffic still used endpoint DNS previously

leo: hypothesis: the interface endpoint ENI IPs rotated after instance replacement at 05:40 UTC; the alias was recreated but the infra PHZ stale A record was added/changed in the morning during a deploy, which took precedence due to resolver rule order

oliver: quick checks: - endpoint ENIs are healthy and attached - security group for endpoint allows 443 from VPC CIDR - route tables for subnets have no blackhole - VPC setting enableDnsHostnames=true, enableDnsSupport=true

michael: commands I ran: ```aws ec2 describe-network-interfaces --filters Name=description,Values="AWS PrivateLink*redis*" --query 'NetworkInterfaces[*].{ID:NetworkInterfaceId,PrivIp:PrivateIpAddress,SG:Groups[*].GroupName}'``` found ENIs 10.1.12.45,10.2.14.33

sara: workaround applied at 06:25 UTC: associated the services-account private hosted zone (ZONE-B) to the VPC so the alias to the endpoint becomes authoritative; sanity checks show pods now resolving to 10.1.12.45

infra-oncall: confirming app errors dropped to <1% after assoc. Rolling a small PR to remove the forwarding resolver rule that pointed to infra-account PHZ to avoid priority inversion

leo: note — the infra-account team created a catch-all PHZ for "prod.internal" last quarter for shared records. That PHZ wasn't supposed to include dynamic service records like redis.*. We need clearer ownership and an automation to prevent stale A records for service endpoints

oliver: follow-up: create a script to detect duplicate private hosted zones and alert if a non-owner zone has A/ALIAS records pointing at IPs in another account. Filing INFRA-3247 to implement

michael: for postmortem: timeline + who changed which hosted zone record + resolver rule priority graph. Assigning to @leo and @sara

aws-bot: incident closed: temporary fix applied (hosts resolving to endpoint ENIs). Please remember to cleanup the stale records in ZONE-A and remove the svc-forward-prod resolver rule after approvals :thumbsup:

oliver: next steps: patch to change our deploy hooks to avoid creating records in infra PHZ, and add a preflight that checks for existing PHZ ownership. Also schedule a 1hr sync with infra-account owners tomorrow 14:00 UTC

michael: thanks all — marking thread resolved for now, leaving INFRA-3247 + followups in triage
